title: Recover from a Poisoned Mutex
goal: Access the protected data inside a Mutex even after another thread panicked.

source.attribution: adapted from Day 4 Afternoon: Shared State

hints: When a thread panics while holding a lock, lock() returns Err(PoisonError).
PoisonError carries the MutexGuard inside it, which you can extract with into_inner().
explanation: mutex.lock() returns Err(PoisonError) if a thread panicked while holding the mutex. Calling into_inner() on PoisonError retrieves the underlying MutexGuard, allowing data access. Calling panic! terminates execution rather than recovering the value, and err.get_ref() returns &MutexGuard, causing a match arm type mismatch.
